prompt: Where does `.resizable()` go when you use `AsyncImage(url:content:placeholder:)`?

choices.text: On `AsyncImage` itself, before `.frame`
choices.why: `AsyncImage` is not an `Image`; Apple's documentation says the modifier cannot go there.

choices.text: On the `Image` the content closure receives
choices.why: Right: the closure hands you the loaded image to modify.

choices.text: On the placeholder, which then sizes the image
choices.why: The placeholder is drawn only while loading.

choices.text: Nowhere: `AsyncImage` resizes to its frame by itself
choices.why: Without `resizable` the picture is drawn at its own pixel size and cropped.

prompt: On iOS 17, does `AsyncImage` promise to keep a cover it has already downloaded?
hint: Apple's documentation dates the caching to a later iOS.

choices.text: Yes, in a memory cache shared by every `AsyncImage`
choices.why: No such cache is promised on iOS 17.

choices.text: Yes, on disk, for as long as the app is installed
choices.why: Nothing promises that either.

choices.text: No; iOS 27 is where HTTP caching is documented
choices.why: Right, which is why section 06 builds a cache the app controls.

choices.text: No, and it downloads every cover twice on purpose
choices.why: It may download again; nothing does it twice on purpose.

prompt: A cover's download fails, and the placeholder is an `Image` that does not load either. What does the person see?

choices.text: Nothing, and no error is reported
choices.why: Right: which is why the phase form, with a `failure` case, exists.

choices.text: A red error symbol drawn by SwiftUI
choices.why: SwiftUI draws nothing of its own here.

choices.text: An alert saying the image could not be loaded
choices.why: `AsyncImage` never shows an alert.

choices.text: The last cover that loaded in that row
choices.why: Nothing keeps an old picture in its place.

prompt: How many bytes does a 1200 by 800 cover take once decoded?
The photograph downloaded as 40,614 bytes. Why did it decode to 48,771,072?

choices.text: The PNG was corrupted and decoded wrongly
choices.why: Its header was read correctly: 4032 by 3024.

choices.text: The server sent it uncompressed
choices.why: It arrived as 40,614 bytes, compressed.

choices.text: Four bytes for each of 4032 x 3024 pixels
choices.why: Right: memory follows the pixels, not the file.

choices.text: Swift keeps ten copies of every image it decodes
choices.why: One copy; it is simply large.

prompt: An 80-point square on a 3x screen: how many pixels wide is it?
A real photograph of the same 4032 by 3024 size compresses to 3 MB rather than 40 KB. What happens to its decoded size?
hint: What does the decoded size depend on?

choices.text: It grows about seventy times, with the file
choices.why: The file's size does not enter the arithmetic.

choices.text: Nothing: still 48,771,072 bytes
choices.why: Right: same pixels, same memory.

choices.text: It shrinks, because the detail compresses into fewer pixels
choices.why: The pixel count is in the header and does not change.

choices.text: It cannot be known without decoding it
choices.why: The header says width and height, and that is enough.

prompt: What does downsampling with ImageIO change?

choices.text: The file the server sends

choices.text: How many pixels are decoded
choices.why: Right: only the ones the screen needs.

choices.text: How the frame scales the picture when it draws
choices.why: That is what `AsyncImage` does, after decoding everything.

choices.text: The colour depth, from four bytes a pixel to one
choices.why: Each pixel still takes four bytes; there are fewer of them.

prompt: Match each ImageIO option to what it does.

pairs.right: Do not decode the whole image when opening it
The longer side of the result, in pixels
Decode now, on the calling thread

prompt: Why does the downsampling run where the download ran, and not when the row draws?

choices.text: ImageIO cannot be called from SwiftUI files
choices.why: It can be called from anywhere; where it runs is the question.

choices.text: Because the download keeps the file open
choices.why: The data is in memory; no file is open.

choices.text: Decoding a big photograph on the main actor drops frames while the list scrolls
choices.why: Right: CPU work belongs off the main actor, and only the small result crosses.

choices.text: Downsampling needs the network to be available
choices.why: It works on bytes already downloaded.

prompt: Ten rows asked for three covers at once, and `covers` printed `3 downloads`. What prevented the other seven?
hint: They all asked before any download had finished.

choices.text: `NSCache`, which had the covers already
choices.why: Nothing was cached yet when they asked; the downloads were still running.

choices.text: The `inFlight` dictionary
choices.why: Right: later rows awaited the download already under way.

choices.text: `URLSession`, which merges identical requests
choices.why: It sends what it is given.

choices.text: The server, which refused repeated requests with 304
choices.why: The server answered every request it got; only three were sent.

prompt: Why are `inFlight` and `downloads` updated before the first `await` in `data(for:)`?
hint: An actor runs one method at a time only between suspensions.

choices.text: So no other caller sees an empty slot and starts a second download
choices.why: Right: at an `await` another call runs in between, and by then the slot is taken.

choices.text: Because the compiler refuses an assignment after `await`
choices.why: It allows them; the order is a choice.

choices.text: To make the counter match the server's log
choices.why: The order matters for correctness, not for logs.

choices.text: Because `NSCache` must be written to first
choices.why: The cache is written after the download.

prompt: With a 50 MB limit, what did the cache keep once all three covers had been downloaded?

choices.text: All three
choices.why: Together they passed the limit.

choices.text: The two covers, since they are cheaper
choices.why: It went the other way.

choices.text: The photograph only
choices.why: Right: the one picture the list least needed at full size.

choices.text: Nothing, because the limit was passed
choices.why: It evicted until it fitted.

prompt: Which cache keeps responses on disk according to the server's HTTP headers?

choices.text: `NSCache`

choices.text: `URLCache`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `ImageCache`
choices.why: The planner's cache is in memory and decides by cost.

choices.text: `UserDefaults`
choices.why: That stores small preferences, not responses.

prompt: Why is `images: ImageCache` passed into `CourseRow` instead of created inside it?

choices.text: A cache per row would share nothing

choices.text: To make the row testable on Linux

choices.text: Because `List` destroys anything a row creates

prompt: A row scrolls away while its cover downloads. `task(id:)` is cancelled. What happens to the download?

choices.text: It is restarted at a lower priority
choices.why: Nothing restarts it.

choices.text: `URLSession` pauses it until the row reappears
choices.why: Nothing pauses it.
